title: FINANCIAL ANALYSIS AND CONTROL OF PUBLIC PROCUREMENT
summary: The article is devoted to the study of the phenomena of financial control, audit and analysis in the context of their use as part of the toolkit for regulating public procurement at the macro level of the state. Auditing of public procurement becomes one of the types of control by the state and guarantees the reliability of bidding. The development of social relations and the introduction of martial law in Ukraine sets its own requirements for public procurement and, accordingly, forms various control results. The relevance of the study lies in the need for state regulation of public procurement as a set of organizational, economic and legal methods and tools, general and specific, with the help of which interconnected functions are performed to ensure purposeful, continuous, effective influence of the state on processes and procedures in the country for the needs of sustainable functioning and development of the economy. The hypothesis of the scientific study consists in justifying the importance of implementing the toolkit of finan­cial control and analysis within the framework of a systematic, structured process of state regu­lation, optimized for Ukraine in view of the conditions of the external and internal environ­ment (restrictions, problems and opportunities) that appear in order to promote the realization of the potential of the national economy. A system of measures aimed at improving financial control and analysis of public procurement is proposed. The authors of the article: developed a scheme of regulated measures aimed at improving financial control and analysis of public procurement; typical violations that arise as a result of public procurement audits are summarized and a model of risk audit organization and decision-making during public procurement is formed. The authors make proposals for the development of a system of measures aimed at improving financial control and analysis of public procurement, which ensure greater transparency, efficiency and honesty by improving the system of financial control and analysis at the level of procurement monitoring. The conducted scientific research is confirmed by statistical data, on the basis of the analysis of which conclusions were formed.

title: Green tourism and sustainable development in ASEAN-5: Evidence from panel data
summary: Tourism plays an important role in supporting sustainable development in ASEAN; however, its expansion can also generate environmental pressures that may undermine long-term sustainability. Green tourism offers an approach to balancing tourism development with environmental conservation and resource efficiency. This study examines the relationship between green tourism and sustainable development in five ASEAN countries—Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam—during the 2006–2021 period. Green tourism is proxied by the Environmental Performance Index (EPI), Travel and Tourism Development Index (TTDI), and Renewable Energy Consumption (REC), while Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is included as a control variable. The Sustainable Development Index (SDI) is used as the dependent variable. Using panel data regression, the Fixed Effects Model (FEM) is selected as the most appropriate estimation approach. The results indicate that EPI and TTDI have positive and statistically significant relationships with SDI, suggesting that stronger environmental performance and tourism development are associated with higher levels of sustainable development. In contrast, REC and GDP show negative and statistically significant relationships with SDI. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening environmental governance, improving sustainable tourism competitiveness, and accelerating the transition toward cleaner energy systems. The study provides empirical evidence that can support policymakers in designing integrated tourism and environmental strategies to advance sustainable development across ASEAN-5 countries.

title: The Impact of Analyst Earnings Forecast Pressure on Corporate ESG greenwashing
summary: Against the backdrop of the deepening ESG investment philosophy and the advancement of China’s "dual carbon" strategy, the scale of ESG information disclosure by Chinese listed companies has expanded rapidly. However, strategic disclosure practices such as ESG greenwashing have also emerged as a prominent issue constraining the high-quality development of the ESG market. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2012 to 2024, this paper empirically examines the effect, functioning mechanism, and heterogeneity characteristics of analyst earnings forecast pressure on corporate ESG greenwashing behavior. The study finds that analyst earnings forecast pressure significantly exacerbates the degree of corporate ESG greenwashing. Mechanism tests show that analyst earnings forecast pressure intensifies corporate financing constraints, driving firms to polish their external image through ESG greenwashing. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that this promoting effect is more pronounced in smaller firms and firms not audited by Big 4 accounting firms. This paper extends the research on the economic consequences of external analyst earnings forecast pressure and the drivers of ESG greenwashing, providing insights for regulators to improve the ESG information disclosure assurance mechanism and promote substantive ESG development among enterprises.

title: Systematic mapping of academic literature on REDD+ in Mexico: research gaps and ways forward
summary: Abstract Academic literature has extensively analyzed REDD+, with some studies criticizing its effectiveness, efficiency, and equity, and others proposing recommendations to improve implementation and outcomes. Mexico was among the pioneering countries in REDD+ implementation, introducing legislative reforms (2008), launching pilot initiatives (2011–2015), and publishing its national REDD+ strategy (2017). However, the country did not progress toward the performance-based payment phase as planned. Despite substantial scholarly attention and several topical review articles, no systematic review of academic literature on REDD+ has focused exclusively on Mexico. This study addresses this gap through a systematic mapping of the scientific literature on REDD+ in Mexico. The objectives were to identify thematic and methodological research gaps, systematize policy and practice recommendations, and assess the feasibility of conducting a full systematic review or a meta-analysis. Our findings on the evolution and geographic distribution of REDD+ studies indicate a link between national policy processes and implementation dynamics that may have generated research opportunities through pilot activities, institutional collaborations, and funding. Among ten broad topics, three dominated the literature: carbon estimation and assessment, environmental governance, and public policies design. Carbon estimation and assessment studies are largely quantitative; however, the feasibility of meta-analysis is constrained by inconsistent reporting and the absence of standardized outcome indicators. In contrast, governance and public policies studies are predominantly qualitative and exploratory or descriptive. Longitudinal and evaluative studies remain scarce, and the lack of standardized social indicators limits systematic cross-case comparison and assessment of institutional change over time. Overall, the trajectory of REDD+ research in Mexico reflects broader trends in environmental governance scholarship, moving from an initial focus on institutional design and participation toward greater attention to impact evaluation. The existing academic literature on REDD+ in Mexico provides a rich but methodologically heterogeneous evidence, suitable for qualitative synthesis but still insufficiently standardized for rigorous meta-analysis.

title: Can Energy Intensity Targets Improve Energy Efficiency in Chinese Cities?
summary: Within China’s target-oriented governance framework, energy intensity targets constitute an important binding instrument through which local governments pursue energy conservation. Using city-level energy intensity target data for China from 2006 to 2022, this study empirically examines the relationship between energy intensity targets and urban energy efficiency. The results show that higher energy intensity target levels are significantly associated with greater urban energy efficiency. The benchmark estimates indicate that a one-percentage-point increase in the energy intensity target is associated with a 0.007-point increase in the urban energy efficiency score, equivalent to approximately 2.0% of the sample mean. Panel quantile estimates further show that the positive relationship between energy intensity targets and energy efficiency is stronger among cities located at higher points of the energy efficiency distribution. The mechanism analysis indicates that reductions in energy consumption, increases in fiscal expenditure on science and technology, and greater green innovation constitute important channels through which energy intensity targets enhance urban energy efficiency. Heterogeneity analysis further shows that the effect is more pronounced in northern cities, non-resource-based cities, small- and medium-sized cities, and cities facing lower economic growth target pressure. This study identifies the relationship between energy intensity target levels and comprehensive energy input–output efficiency at the city level and provides new empirical evidence on how the target responsibility system affects energy governance performance through local government behaviour.

title: How do different forms of environmental regulation affect high-quality economic development?
summary: Environmental regulation is increasingly important for coordinating ecological protection and economic transformation, yet its influence on high-quality economic development (HQED) may differ across regulatory forms. Drawing on institutional theory, this study examines formal and informal environmental regulation across 31 Chinese provinces from 2005 to 2022. Province and year fixed effects are employed together with nonlinear, robustness, heterogeneity, and mechanism analyses. The findings show that formal environmental regulation significantly restrains HQED, whereas informal regulation promotes it. Formal regulation displays a U-shaped effect, while informal regulation follows an inverted U-shaped pattern, with both nonlinear relationships mainly evident in eastern China. Mechanism tests further show that technological innovation and industrial agglomeration help transmit the effects of environmental regulation to HQED. These findings demonstrate that the economic consequences of environmental governance depend on regulatory form and provide evidence for designing differentiated environmental policies that support sustainable economic transformation.

title: Service-oriented transformation breeds digital catering: variation by ownership
summary: Purpose The literature has attributed enterprise digital catering to corporate finance and corporate governance factors, including operational pressure and individual or organizational characteristics; however, the role played by enterprise strategy in this context has been overlooked. From the perspective of enterprise ownership, this study examines the heterogeneous effects of service-oriented transformation on digital catering and identifies the moderating roles played by public attention, equity incentives, and information transparency in this context. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a propensity score matching difference-in-differences method to examine how service-oriented transformation influences digital catering and explores the underlying mechanisms from the perspective of ownership. The study uses panel data obtained from Chinese listed manufacturing enterprises between 2010 and 2023. Findings The effect of service-oriented transformation on digital catering varies across different ownership structures. Service-oriented transformation stimulates digital catering among state-owned enterprises (SOEs) but has no statistically significant effect on non-SOEs. These findings indicate that SOEs have strong incentives to engage in digital catering because of their affiliation with the government administrative system. Further analysis reveals that, in the context of internal governance, both equity incentives and information transparency weaken the stimulating effect of service-oriented transformation on digital catering. In contrast, external public attention strengthens this effect. Social implications This study helps both policymakers and regulators understand the key drivers of enterprise digital catering in contexts involving policy-driven service-oriented transformation. These findings provide implications for regulating opportunistic disclosure practices and encouraging manufacturing enterprises to undertake substantive transformation. Originality/value This study addresses the gap in enterprise digital catering research related to strategic perspectives. It extends catering theory to the context of digitalization and deepens our understanding of how enterprises that exhibit different ownership structures respond differently to service-oriented transformation. The findings also provide empirical evidence to support a theoretical framework that links strategic transformation with noneconomic behavior. Additionally, this study has policy implications for efforts to implement service-oriented transformation and promote a sustainable digitalization.

title: Perspectives on the Iberian Economic Integration
summary: This paper examines the functioning of the European Single Market through the experience of Spain and Portugal, two economies whose geographical proximity, shared border and joint EU membership since 1986 make them a particularly informative case study. Organizing the analysis around the Single Market’s four freedoms, the paper combines descriptive indicators, structural-gravity estimates, a multi-country general-equilibrium trade model, price-convergence and electricity-coupling measures, administrative labour-market data, survival analysis and granular investment and banking data to assess integration in trade, energy, labour mobility and capital markets. The findings show that Iberian integration is substantial but markedly uneven across dimensions. Trade in goods and production network linkages have deepened considerably since accession, and wholesale electricity markets are exceptionally well integrated, reflecting strong complementarities between Spanish solar and Portuguese hydropower generation. By contrast, services trade, labour mobility and non-bank financial investment remain comparatively underdeveloped. These results show that the legal framework of the Single Market has generated deep integration in some markets while leaving others fragmented, and that closing the remaining gaps requires more effective implementation, regulatory cooperation and mutual recognition, supported by infrastructure investment and interoperable administrative systems.

title: EXAMINING THE ROLE OF STRUCTURAL TRANSFORMATION AND RENEWABLE ENERGY ON SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN KAZAKHSTAN
summary: This study examines whether Kazakhstan's structural transformation has been environmentally sustainable and whether renewable energy can support a greener development trajectory. The study constructs a structural transformation index through principal component analysis, integrating economic growth, urbanization, education, institutional quality, and political stability. The study used the autoregressive distributed lag model to examine the short run and long relationship between the structural transformation, renewable energy and sustainable development in Kazakhstan. The findings of the study indicate that renewable energy has positive and significant effect on sustainable development, highlighting its importance for cleaner environment and sustainable development. In contrast, structural transformation index has negative and significant effect on sustainable development, indicating that Kazakhstan prevailing development has not been sufficiently aligned with environmental sustainability. The results show that economic and institution development alone does not promote sustainable development, when structural transformation remains associated with environmental pressure and fossil fuel dependence. The study suggests the need to accelerate renewable energy adoption, strengthen the environmental governance, promote the green structural transformation and reduce fossil fuel dependence.

title: Reconstructing Digital Sovereignty through State Resilience Legal Policy: Citizen Protection after the Cyberattack on Indonesia’s Temporary National Data Center
summary: The development of information technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) has shifted the paradigm of state resilience away from protection oriented toward territorial areas and toward the protection of a borderless digital space. This shift presents new challenges for the state in protecting its citizens, as reflected in the cyberattack on Indonesia's Temporary National Data Center (PDNS) in 2024. Although Indonesia already has various regulations concerning information technology, cybersecurity, and personal data protection, national legal policy has not yet been fully able to build an integrated framework to respond to digital threats in the AI era. This research aims to analyze the legal policy of state resilience in protecting citizens through a case study of the cyberattack on PDNS, and to reconstruct legal policy based on Digital Sovereignty as a paradigm for strengthening state resilience. This research uses the normative legal research method with statutory, conceptual, and case approaches. The results show that the national legal framework remains sectoral in nature and has not been able to comprehensively integrate cybersecurity governance, data protection, and the use of AI. Therefore, this research offers a reconstruction of legal policy based on Digital Sovereignty, which places control over data, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, and AI governance as a new foundation for strengthening state resilience while guaranteeing the protection of citizens' constitutional rights in the era of digital transformation. The proposed model integrates data sovereignty, infrastructure resilience, AI accountability, supply chain security, and digital human capacity through preventive, adaptive, rights based governance mechanisms for public institutions.

title: R3-GenAI Chat: A Self-Hosted Multimodal RAG Framework with Pre-Retrieval RBAC-ABAC Access Control and Risk-Adaptive Response Governance for Enterprise Documents
summary: Abstract—In this paper, we propose a secure and efficient attribute-based access control system for sensitive documents in cloud environments. The system integrates access control policies with document sensitivity classification and behavior analysis to support fine-grained authorization decisions. We also present a model for handling document operations, auditing, and policy enforcement in a distributed setting. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach improves access control effectiveness and provides better support for sensitive information management in cloud-based document systems.

title: Leading from the middle: how mid-level managers shape digital strategy and innovation
summary: Purpose This study examines how mid-level managers facilitate digital transformation in large incumbent firms and identifies the managerial mechanisms through which they connect strategic digital ambitions with organizational and operational implementation. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts an inductive qualitative research design based on 27 in-depth interviews with mid-level managers from large, stock-listed German firms. The data were analyzed using the Gioia methodology to develop an empirically grounded framework. Findings The findings identify three interrelated aggregate dimensions through which mid-level managers enable digital transformation: strategic orchestration, organizational enablement, and operational integration. Mid-level managers act as a bidirectional interface between strategy and execution by translating strategic objectives into operational action while simultaneously feeding implementation experiences, barriers, and emerging opportunities back into strategic adaptation. Research limitations/implications The study focuses on large German listed companies, limiting the transferability of the findings to SMEs, privately held firms, or organizations operating in different national contexts. As an inductive qualitative study based on interviews, the findings reflect participants’ perspectives and are not statistically generalizable. Future research should examine the proposed framework in different organizational settings, include additional stakeholder groups, and employ quantitative approaches to validate the identified managerial mechanisms and examine their influence on digital transformation outcomes. Practical implications The findings demonstrate that successful digital transformation depends on empowering mid-level managers as connectors between strategy and operations. Organizations should strengthen their strategic, communication, integration, and change management capabilities while equipping them with sufficient technological understanding. Managers should actively align digital initiatives with business objectives, foster employee engagement, support capability development, and promote continuous improvement. The framework provides practical guidance for executives seeking to enhance digital transformation by leveraging the unique intermediary position of mid-level managers throughout the implementation process. Social implications By improving the effectiveness of digital transformation, organizations can better prepare employees for technological change, strengthen organizational learning, and foster more collaborative and adaptive workplaces. The study highlights the importance of communication, employee engagement, and capability development in reducing resistance to change and supporting sustainable organizational transformation, thereby contributing to healthier organizational environments during periods of technological disruption. Originality/value The study advances research on middle management and digital transformation by moving beyond established perspectives on managerial roles, competencies, and leadership behaviors. It develops an integrated framework that explains how strategic, organizational, and operational mechanisms interact throughout digital transformation and highlights the particular relevance of mid-level managers in large incumbent organizations.

title: How ‘Galamsey’ reshapes land, livelihoods, and education in rural Ghana
summary: Illegal small-scale mining, locally known as “galamsey”, has intensified across Ghana, with far-reaching environmental, social and economic consequences for rural communities. Although previous studies have often examined its environmental and livelihood effects separately, less attention has been paid to how these disruptions interact in everyday rural life. This study examines how galamsey reshapes livelihoods, educational participation, environmental wellbeing, and local governance in two mining-affected communities in southern Ghana. Using a qualitative case study design, data were generated through semi-structured interviews with 15 participants, four focus group discussions involving 27 participants, and field observations. The data were analysed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis and interpreted through the Sustainable Livelihoods Framework, Environmental Justice and Political Ecology. The findings show that galamsey constitutes a multidimensional rural development challenge rather than solely an environmental problem. It undermined agricultural livelihoods, increased household insecurity, disrupted children's education, intensified gendered vulnerabilities, reshaped youth aspirations and weakened confidence in environmental governance. The study identifies a double-victim dynamic in which declining livelihood opportunities drew young people into mining, while their participation contributed to the further degradation of resources needed for future livelihoods. Effective responses therefore require integrated, community-centred and justice-oriented approaches combining livelihood diversification, environmental restoration, educational support, youth employment and participatory governance. By showing how environmental degradation, economic insecurity and governance failures reinforce rural vulnerability, the study contributes to debates on sustainable rural development and environmental justice in mining-affected contexts. Galamsey disrupts land, water, livelihoods and schooling, requiring coordinated rather than sector-specific responses. Farmland degradation and unstable household incomes contribute to absenteeism, child labour and gendered vulnerabilities, particularly among girls and young women. Polluted water and unsafe mining landscapes create perceived health risks and weaken children’s educational participation. Inconsistent enforcement, weak accountability and limited community participation undermine trust in environmental governance. Sustainable responses should combine livelihood diversification, educational support, environmental restoration, youth employment and participatory governance.

title: An investigation of the neglected serial mediators and moderators of green inclusive leadership in the hospitality industry
summary: Using social exchange and social identity theories as the theoretical umbrella, our paper proposes and tests the neglected serial mediators and moderators of green inclusive leadership (GIL) using time-lagged data gathered from hospitality employees. The findings from the partial least squares structural equation modeling disclose that employees’ perceptions of green organizational climate (GOC) mediate the influence of GIL on their corporate social responsibility (CSR) judgments. GOC and CSR judgments serially mediate the impact of GIL on their in- and extra-role CSR performances. More importantly, organizational identification strengthens the indirect positive impact of GIL on said CSR performances via GOC and CSR judgments. Our paper augments hospitality literature by extending the understanding of underlying mechanisms (GOC, CSR judgments) and boundary conditions (organizational identification) through which the GIL and CSR outcomes relationship unfolds and contributing to research on sustainable development goals associated with “decent work and economic growth-8” and “responsible consumption and production-12”.

title: The impact of Data assets on price markup
summary: In the digital economy, data assets have become a critical driver of competitive advantage, yet existing literature remains scarce on how these assets influence firms’ market power. Using a sample of China A-share listed firms from 2007 to 2024, this study applies the De Loecker and Warzynski production function approach to estimate firm-level price markups and systematically empirically examines the impact, mechanisms, and economic consequences of data assets on price markups. The findings reveal that data assets significantly elevate firms’ price markups, and this relationship withstands a battery of robustness checks. Mechanism analysis demonstrates that data assets enhance markups through three channels: raising capacity utilization, alleviating financing constraints, and reducing agency costs. Heterogeneity tests show that these effects are more pronounced in non-state-owned enterprises, industries with higher competitive intensity, and regions with more developed data factor market institutions. Finally, the economic consequence analysis confirms that the markup gains driven by data assets substantially boost total factor productivity, thereby empowering firms to pursue high-quality development. This study enriches the microeconomic literature on the role of data as an input factor and provides new empirical evidence on the value-creation mechanisms of data assets, offering important insights for firms’digital transformation strategies and for improving data factor market governance.

title: Digital technology, agricultural resilience, and food security: a mini review
summary: Digital technologies are increasingly deployed to strengthen food security under climate stress, resource constraints, and geopolitical disruption. This review synthesizes two largely separate bodies of scholarship: an international literature on digital agriculture and the four classical dimensions of food security, and a rapidly expanding Chinese literature on the digital economy and agricultural economic resilience. Three claims emerge. First, digital technologies strengthen all four dimensions of food security through distinct mechanisms: (1) availability through productivity and input-use efficiency gains, which operate mainly through institutional intermediation, including land transfer, socialized services, industrial integration, and human capital, rather than through adoption alone; (2) access through market information and digital finance; (3) stability through traceability, early-warning systems, and insurance; (4) and utilization through traceability, nutrition information, and mobile payments. Second, quasi-experimental evidence shows that digital infrastructure, digital finance, and artificial intelligence raise the resilience of grain production and value chains, mainly through socialized services, land transfer, industrial integration, and human capital rather than adoption alone. Third, the benefits are conditional and unevenly distributed: the direction of spatial spillovers depends on absorptive capacity, market integration, and factor mobility.

title: THE HISTORICAL EMERGENCE AND EVOLUTION OF ENVIRONMENTAL LAW IN NIGERIA: A CRITICAL APPRAISAL
summary: Abstract:The development of environmental law in Nigeria has evolved from pre-colonial and colonial eras of conservationist policies to more comprehensive pieces of legislation (post-independence era) aimed at addressing environmental degradation that guarantee sustainable development. This paper traces the history, X-raying the emergence of environmental law in Nigeria through examining key milestones, statutory enactments, judicial interventions, and perspectives of legal luminaries/scholars in the field of environmental law. In addition, it underscores the challenges that hinder the enforcement of available legislation and policies, as well as the influence of international treaties on Nigeria's environmental legislation and policy structure. The study underscores robust legal frameworks and enforcement mechanisms as pivotal in protecting Nigeria's environment for future generations. It also evaluates the constitutional foundation of environmental governance in Nigeria, particularly the relevance of Chapter II of the 1999 Constitution and its justiciability debates. The paper critically assesses the role of regulatory bodies, compliance monitoring mechanisms, and community participation in environmental decision-making processes. Furthermore, it reflects on the persistent problems of weak institutional capacity, political interference, corruption, inadequate funding, and limited public awareness, which collectively undermine effective enforcement. The study situates Nigeria’s environmental legal regime within broader global sustainability discourse and highlights the need for legislative reforms, strengthened judicial oversight, and improved synergy between domestic laws and international environmental obligations.

title: Machine Learning Meets Blockchain: A Domain-Oriented Review of Integration Mechanisms, Applications, and Open Challenges
summary: Blockchain and machine learning (ML) are combined in systems that must learn from multi-party data and keep a verifiable record of what was used and decided. This scoping-style review of a ranked sample covers seven domains: healthcare, finance, supply chain, energy, smart contracts, transportation and education. We searched Scopus and IEEE Xplore on 15 October 2026, ranked 5,195 candidate records, read 345 abstracts in rank order, coded a core corpus of 192 studies and read 38 in full. Federated learning is the most common method (93 of 192 core studies name it), and detection of fraud, intrusions and vulnerabilities is the most common task among the 38. None of the 38 reports a deployment, 24 report a measured ledger figure and two measure ledger energy. Ten use more than one privacy mechanism, and only two report accuracy with and without it. Attack tests are small, and one study tests a Sybil attacker. Studies differ too much to compare, so we do not rank domains. A ledger shows that a record has not changed, not that it was correct when written. The main gaps are realistic evaluation, shared benchmarks and reporting standards, and tested explanations for decisions made inside contracts.

title: Low-altitude economy, vertical spatial transformation and pathways for pollution and carbon emission reduction: policy and social evidence from Chinese provinces
summary: As an emerging industry paradigm, the alignment between policy regulation of the low-altitude economy and regional achievements in pollution and carbon emission reduction constitutes a critical issue for promoting industrial green transformation and achieving sustainable development. Using panel data from 28 Chinese provinces over the period 2008–2023, this study systematically examines the nonlinear impact of low-altitude economic policy intensity on regional pollution and carbon emission reduction and its underlying mechanisms. Additionally, it analyzes the driving effects of the low-altitude economy on spatial transformation from pathway restructuring, spatial asymmetry, and risk resonance. The findings reveal that:(1) The results indicate that the impact of low-altitude economy policy intensity on pollution and carbon emission levels exhibits a nonlinear pattern, an estimated empirical transition point of approximately 2.896. (2) Low-altitude economy policy intensity first weakens and then strengthens environmental regulation, while its promoting effect on green innovation gradually diminishes, thereby shaping its pollution and carbon emission reduction effects. (3) A stronger low-altitude airspace flight foundation accelerates the crossing of the turning point and strengthens environmental benefits. (4) The spatial effects are uneven. Provinces such as Sichuan, Jilin, Shaanxi, and Zhejiang exhibit heterogeneous transitions in the marginal environmental effects of low-altitude economy development during key development stages. (5) Spatial transformation is asymmetric, with stronger pollution and carbon reduction effects in regions with better ecological endowments or higher climate risk exposure. (6) Public attention to the low-altitude economy and carbon market returns exhibit a negative risk resonance over short-to-medium-term horizons (100–150 days; 12–24 cycles), indicating time-scale dependence. Overall, the results reveal stage-dependent and spatially differentiated environmental consequences of the low-altitude economy, providing new evidence for understanding the carbon-management implications of emerging spatial economic activities.

title: Grassroots Environmental Discourse and the National Project “Ecological Well-Being”: Topic Modeling of Russian VKontakte Communities
summary: Effective environmental governance increasingly depends on aligning top-down policy priorities with grassroots civic practices. This study assesses the potential for integrating grassroots environmental initiatives into Russia’s National Project “Ecological Well-Being” by comparing the thematic structure of VKontakte environmental communities with six federal project areas. A corpus of 64,364 posts obtained in 2025 by 201 long-running environmental communities was collected and balanced to 30,500 texts. BERTopic, using multilingual sentence embeddings, UMAP, and HDBSCAN, assigned 15,066 posts (49.4% of the balanced corpus) to 397 stable thematic clusters, while the remaining 15,434 posts were treated as noise and excluded from the thematic comparison. Topic labels and correspondence with the National Project initiatives were subsequently assessed with DeepSeek Chat. Gap Analysis showed that 64 of the 397 topics (16.12%), comprising 3081 of the 15,066 clustered posts (20.45%), directly overlapped with at least one initiative of the National Project. The remaining 333 topics (83.88%), comprising 11,985 clustered posts (79.55%), formed a Grassroots Surplus outside the formal policy agenda. The largest overlap in terms of both topics and posts concerned biodiversity (12.34% of topics; 15.46% of posts) and the circular economy (4.79%; 5.27%, respectively), while the clean air initiative had the lowest representation (0.25%; 0.14%). Animal welfare, school and family environmental initiatives, and local recreation emerged as gateway topics that may connect everyday civic practices with national environmental programs.

title: Better together: a narrative review of academia and medical device industry collaborations toward sustainable kidney care
summary: Abstract Background Chronic kidney disease is a leading cause of death and disability globally, with the greatest burden and most limited access to kidney therapies in low- and middle-income countries. Environmentally sustainable kidney care is increasingly recognized as essential. Structured, patient-informed collaboration between academia and the kidney medical device industry holds potential toward solving these problems. Methods We conducted a narrative review of partnerships between academia and industry in environmentally sustainable kidney care. A scoping search of PubMed, Google Scholar, CINAHL and the Cochrane Library was combined with targeted grey-literature searches of key organizations. Eligible sources describe partnership structures, governance, financing, environmental or social outcomes, or lessons learned. Findings were synthesized thematically, informed by patient perspective, then interpreted using a United Nations sustainable development partnership framework. Results Existing initiatives and consortia such as the International Society of Nephrology’s GREEN-K, the Kidney Health Initiative and KitNewCare illustrate the potential of multi-stakeholder collaboration to advance sustainable kidney care. Patient organizations, notably the European Kidney Patients’ Federation, emphasise that environmental initiatives must align with treatment quality, patient autonomy and equity. Industry-led innovations include water- and energy-efficient technologies, life-cycle assessment of processes and/or consumables, lower-impact concentrates and operational optimizations. Key barriers include heterogeneous regulatory requirements, limited materials circularity, public procurement that prioritizes cost over sustainability, and financial investments associated with device innovation. We envision partnering opportunities to both improve access to, and environmental sustainability of, kidney therapies. Conclusions Achieving low-carbon, resilient and equitable kidney care requires academia–industry partnerships that embed meaningful patient involvement, position industry as co-creator, and align incentives around shared clinical and environmental goals. Structured partnering frameworks can support transparent governance, harmonised metrics and scalable green innovation across the kidney medical device sector.

title: Examining Agents’ Activities in Football: A Comparison between Türkiye and England
summary: The aim of this study is to compare football agent activities in Türkiye and England within financial, administrative, and legal contexts. The study employs a qualitative research design, utilizing document analysis, purposive sampling for data collection, and content analysis methods. The documents collected as raw data include football agent regulations, lists of licensed football agents, agent payments, and agent payment reports publicly shared by the Turkish Football Federation and the English Football Association. The findings indicate that significantly higher amounts of agent fees are paid in England compared to Türkiye. While all clubs in England declare agent payments, the number of clubs reporting such payments in Türkiye is considerably limited. In addition, while data on women’s football is available in England, no such data exists for Türkiye. Furthermore, the number of licensed football agents in England is substantially higher than in Türkiye. The results of the study reveal that England operates a more transparent system compared to Türkiye. This is attributed to the more effective management of information processes in England. In Türkiye, the high number of unlicensed football agents leads to off-the-record activities, which are not reflected in official reports. Similarly, in terms of auditing processes, England demonstrates a more effective and systematic structure compared to Türkiye

title: Does the digital financial literacy impact on effective investment decisions? The mediating role of financial inclusion
summary: Digital Financial Literacy (DFL) is the ability to handle and navigate financial activities using digital technologies and platforms. With the growth of FinTech and the shift in policies of the government in India, the need to understand the influence of DFL on investment decisions has become increasingly important. This study examines the impact of digital financial literacy on investment goals (ING) and examines the mediating role of financial inclusion (FI) and financial decision-making. The research also incorporates such considerations as subjective norms, perceived behavioral control, and financial accessibility to improve understanding of investment decisions. Data collection took place via surveys distributed among 232 people in India from May 2024 to August 2025. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) were used in the validation of the measurement model through reliability and construct validation, whereas CB-SEM was used to identify the structural relationships between the variables under investigation. Fit quality was determined using conventional metrics such as CFI, TLI, and RMSEA. It was found out that digital financial literacy positively affects the decision to invest (p < 0.05), while financial inclusion acts as a mediator between financial decision-making and investment. These findings highlight the importance of enhancing digital financial literacy and strengthening financial inclusion to support informed investment decisions

title: Analisis Kesesuaian Laporan Keuangan UMKM Dee Rumah Cake & Catering dengan SAK ETAP
summary: This study aims to analyze the extent to which the financial statements of the MSME "Dee Rumah Cake & Catering" align with the Financial Accounting Standards for Entities without Public Accountability (SAK ETAP). The study is motivated by the fact that many MSME operators have yet to implement formal financial reporting systems that meet established standards; consequently, the financial information produced lacks the full relevance and reliability required to support decision-making or facilitate access to financing. A qualitative descriptive approach, utilizing a case study method, was employed. The data analyzed include the financial statements of Dee Rumah Cake & Catering—comprising the income statement, statement of changes in equity, balance sheet, and statement of cash flows—along with other relevant supporting data. Data were collected through documentation and a literature review, while the analysis involved comparing the components, recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure of the financial statements against the provisions of SAK ETAP. The findings indicate that the financial statements of Dee Rumah Cake & Catering are not yet fully compliant with SAK ETAP. This non-compliance stems from incomplete financial statement components—specifically the absence of Notes to the Financial Statements (CaLK)—inconsistent recording and disclosure of fixed assets, misclassification of transactions within the statement of cash flows, and a lack of sufficient supporting documentation for transactions. As a result, the current financial statements remain overly simplistic and fail to fully satisfy the presentation principles mandated by SAK ETAP. This study is intended to provide recommendations for the MSME owner to enhance their understanding of accounting and implement SAK ETAP more comprehensively, thereby ensuring that financial statements become more informative and serve as a more effective basis for decision-making.

title: From AI Adoption to Institutional Preparedness: Governing Enterprises for AGI
summary: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) is increasingly discussed not merely as a technical frontier but as a social and institutional challenge. Drawing on current generative and agentic AI as diagnostic evidence, this paper examines enterprise institutional preparedness for increasingly general and autonomous AI systems through three interrelated dimensions: organizational resilience, employee protection, and social responsibility. Using conceptual and normative analysis, the paper synthesizes AI governance, organizational resilience, labor studies, corporate social responsibility, and policy frameworks to develop a forward-looking governance architecture. The framework links three levels of institutional exposure: continuity of organizational functions, preservation of worker agency, and external social legitimacy. It identifies seven preparedness components: strategic foresight, governance architecture, risk and impact assessment, human oversight, employee protection, social responsibility, and continuous learning. The analysis further distinguishes scalable risks already visible in current AI from potentially discontinuous risks associated with greater autonomy and cross-domain integration. The study shifts the unit of analysis from tool-level AI risk management to enterprise-level institutional capacity to preserve organizational continuity, worker agency, and external social legitimacy.

title: Evaluating Social Innovation Program through the Social Return on Investment (SROI) Method: A Case Study of the KIJANGKU Program at PT TMMIN Karawang Plant 1-2
summary: The shift of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) from a voluntary commitment to a business strategy and regulatory obligation has increased the need for measurable assessments of the social and environmental impacts of corporate sustainability initiatives. This study evaluates the effectiveness and the social, economic, and environmental value created by the KIJANGKU (Konservasi Hijau Selamatkan Lingkunganku) Social Innovation Program, implemented by PT Toyota Motor Manufacturing Indonesia (TMMIN) at Karawang Plants 1–2 during 2023–2025. Using the Social Return on Investment (SROI) approach, the study assesses the value generated relative to the program’s social investment. A total investment of IDR 381,000,000 (present value: IDR 399,237,600) produced benefits with a present value of IDR 524,762,076, yielding an SROI ratio of 1.31. Each IDR 1 invested thus generated approximately IDR 1.31 in social, economic, and environmental value. The findings indicate that KIJANGKU benefited local communities while supporting environmental conservation and sustainability. The study highlights the applicability of SROI for evaluating the broader impacts of corporate social innovation programs and their contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), including SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals).

title: Reviving the trade and competition nexus in digital platform governance
summary: Abstract Data-driven advantages facilitate practices that consolidate market power and enable large digital platforms to determine competitive conditions in digital trade. Recent digital competition cases provide useful examples for rethinking the relationship between competition policy and digital trade law in the digital economy. The first part of this article illustrates how domestic competition regimes can have substantial cross-border effects on data flows and digital trade. It argues that domestic measures addressing platform practices such as self-preferencing, bundling, or data-driven discrimination may alter market access conditions for foreign digital service suppliers or redirect data flows across borders. The second part identifies the notable disconnect that persists between competition policy and digital trade law. Although provisions in existing digital trade chapters gradually intersect with competition regulation, such engagement remains peripheral rather than substantive. In addition, modern free trade agreements reflect a structural separation between digital trade liberalization and competition policy. This separation is increasingly difficult to sustain in the context of digital platform governance. The third part examines the drivers and challenges of reviving the trade and competition nexus. It explains why the most recent World Trade Organization Joint Statement Initiative on E-commerce text contains no digital competition disciplines, emphasizing that sector-specific competition disciplines require broad political support from both developed and developing countries, which is currently lacking. It also highlights the core doctrinal challenges in adapting traditional competition law to digital markets. Against this background, the article points out the experimental and incremental approaches under Digital Economy Agreements. Although these developments remain fragmented, soft-law oriented, and primarily cooperation-based, their real function is to facilitate soft-law, non-justiciable coordination as a modest experiment that may inform the development of more substantial competition disciplines in future international trade agreements.

title: How ‘Galamsey’ reshapes land, livelihoods, and education in rural Ghana
summary: Illegal small-scale mining, locally known as “galamsey”, has intensified across Ghana, with far-reaching environmental, social and economic consequences for rural communities. Although previous studies have often examined its environmental and livelihood effects separately, less attention has been paid to how these disruptions interact in everyday rural life. This study examines how galamsey reshapes livelihoods, educational participation, environmental wellbeing, and local governance in two mining-affected communities in southern Ghana. Using a qualitative case study design, data were generated through semi-structured interviews with 15 participants, four focus group discussions involving 27 participants, and field observations. The data were analysed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis and interpreted through the Sustainable Livelihoods Framework, Environmental Justice and Political Ecology. The findings show that galamsey constitutes a multidimensional rural development challenge rather than solely an environmental problem. It undermined agricultural livelihoods, increased household insecurity, disrupted children's education, intensified gendered vulnerabilities, reshaped youth aspirations and weakened confidence in environmental governance. The study identifies a double-victim dynamic in which declining livelihood opportunities drew young people into mining, while their participation contributed to the further degradation of resources needed for future livelihoods. Effective responses therefore require integrated, community-centred and justice-oriented approaches combining livelihood diversification, environmental restoration, educational support, youth employment and participatory governance. By showing how environmental degradation, economic insecurity and governance failures reinforce rural vulnerability, the study contributes to debates on sustainable rural development and environmental justice in mining-affected contexts. Policy highlightsGalamsey disrupts land, water, livelihoods and schooling, requiring coordinated rather than sector-specific responses.Farmland degradation and unstable household incomes contribute to absenteeism, child labour and gendered vulnerabilities, particularly among girls and young women.Polluted water and unsafe mining landscapes create perceived health risks and weaken children’s educational participation.Inconsistent enforcement, weak accountability and limited community participation undermine trust in environmental governance.Sustainable responses should combine livelihood diversification, educational support, environmental restoration, youth employment and participatory governance.

title: Taming the narcissist
summary: Abstract We investigate whether corporate governance constrains the agency costs associated with CEO narcissism. Narcissistic CEOs are linked to lower earnings quality, greater risk‐taking, and inefficient overinvestment. However, these effects vary substantially with board structure. Boards characterized by low diversity and excessive director compensation are significantly less effective at constraining the adverse consequences of CEO narcissism, whereas more diverse boards with appropriately incentivized directors mitigate these effects. The strongest adverse outcomes occur when low board diversity and excessive director compensation coexist. Our findings highlight the central role of governance design in limiting personality‐driven distortions in corporate decision‐making.

title: THE USE OF DIGITAL TECHNOLOGIES IN STUDENT CAREER GUIDANCE
summary: This thesis analyzes the role and potential of modern digital technologies in student career guidance. It highlights the inadequacy of traditional methods in the context of digital transformation and assesses the impact of online testing, digital portfolios, occupational databases, and mobile applications on the effectiveness of career choice. It also substantiates existing technological limitations and promising directions for their integration with artificial intelligence (AI).

title: Endogenous Corporate Social Responsibility in a Congested Network Monopoly: Passive Versus Responsive Consumer Expectations
summary: ABSTRACT This paper examines endogenous corporate social responsibility (CSR) in a monopolistic network industry in which participation generates both network benefits and congestion. We develop a fulfilled‐expectations model and compare the firm's CSR, pricing and output decisions under passive and responsive consumer expectations. Under passive expectations, positive network externalities always sustain CSR, whereas sufficiently strong congestion may eliminate commitment when consumers' sensitivity to CSR is limited. Under responsive expectations, CSR is always strictly positive. Whenever the passive solution is interior, responsive expectations induce stronger CSR under congestion but weaker CSR when positive network benefits dominate. The profit and welfare rankings across expectation regimes similarly depend on the nature of network interactions. Nevertheless, within each regime, endogenous CSR raises monopoly profit, consumer surplus and social surplus relative to the corresponding no‐CSR benchmark whenever it is adopted. These findings remain robust when production involves increasing marginal costs. Allowing for heterogeneous expectations further shows that, under congestion, a sufficiently large share of responsive consumers can eliminate the no‐CSR outcome.

title: Research on the Theoretical Framework of Market-based Allocation of Data Elements
summary: With the advent of the digital economy era, data is increasingly valued as a new factor of production, and the market-based allocation of data elements is an important part of promoting high-quality economic development. Based on the summary of the basic nature and characteristics of data elements, this paper proposes a theoretical model for the market-based allocation of data elements. The article analyzes the four aspects of property rights definition, value assessment, circulation and transaction, and income distribution of data elements, and elaborates on the theoretical and practical problems existing in the market-based allocation of data elements. The article argues that data elements are non-competitive, with increasing returns to scale and strong externalities, which are different from traditional factors of production and pose new challenges to traditional factor market theories. This paper innovatively presents a theoretical framework for market-based allocation of data elements, including a hierarchical data property rights confirmation mechanism, a dynamic value assessment model, and a multi-party collaborative governance framework, and proposes corresponding countermeasures and suggestions for problems such as difficult data rights confirmation, difficult pricing, and difficult trading. The study suggests that to achieve a good market-based allocation of data elements, it is necessary to improve the data property rights system, cultivate the data element market, enhance the efficiency of data resource allocation on the basis of safeguarding personal privacy and protecting data security, give full play to the guiding role of the government, the decisive role of the market, and the joint efforts of all parties to maximize the value of data elements. To boost the quality and efficiency of the real economy.

title: The Effect of Performance-Based Budgeting Systems on Green Innovation Outputs in Private Industrial Firms: The Mediating Role of Digital Transformation and the Moderating Effect of Transformational Leadership
summary: This study investigates the impact of Program and Performance Budgeting (PPB) systems on green innovation outcomes in the Iraqi private industrial sector by examining the mediating role of digital transformation and the dual moderating effect of transformational leadership. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed using a stratified random sample of 520 respondents from 45 Iraqi private industrial firms across five industrial sectors. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with 5,000 bootstrap resamples, along with conditional effects analysis at three levels of transformational leadership. The findings demonstrate that Program and Performance Budgeting has a positive and statistically significant direct effect on green innovation (β = 0.431, p < 0.001) and an even stronger positive effect on digital transformation (β = 0.773, p < 0.001), representing the strongest relationship in the model. Digital transformation also partially mediates the relationship between Program and Performance Budgeting and green innovation (β = 0.201, p < 0.001), indicating that Program and Performance Budgeting promotes green innovation through two distinct pathways: a direct pathway via incentives and accountability mechanisms, and an indirect pathway through the enhancement of digital capabilities. In contrast, the results reveal that transformational leadership does not significantly moderate the direct relationship between Program and Performance Budgeting and green innovation (H5: β = −0.001, p = 0.966). However, it significantly and negatively moderates the relationship between Program and Performance Budgeting and digital transformation (H6: β = −0.029, p = 0.029), suggesting a substitution effect, whereby strong transformational leadership bypasses the budgeting mechanism and independently stimulates digital transformation. Similarly, the index of moderated mediation was statistically significant but negative (H7: β = −0.009, p = 0.033), further supporting the substitution phenomenon in which strong transformational leadership independently drives digital transformation beyond the influence of the budgeting system. The structural model explained 72.4% of the variance in digital transformation and 28.3% of the variance in green innovation. This study presents the first integrated structural model that examines Program and Performance Budgeting as a driver of green innovation in the Iraqi industrial context. By integrating Contingency Theory and Resource Dependence Theory, it reveals an unexpected leadership pattern that reframes the role of transformational leadership in sustainability models within emerging economies.

title: The Inhibitory Mechanism of Financial Investment on Technological Innovation and the Moderating Effect of Managerial Behavior
summary: Innovation is the primary factor driving enterprise development. Based on Chinese A-share non-financial listed companies from 2009 to 2022, this paper employs fixed-effect regression models and heterogeneity tests to empirically examine the impact of corporate financialization on technological innovation. We further introduce managerial overconfidence as a moderating variable to analyze its effect on the relationship between innovation input and output. The results show that corporate financial asset investment significantly inhibits technological innovation, as reflected by simultaneous declines in R&D input and innovation output. Managerial overconfidence mitigates the negative impact of financialization on innovation output to a certain extent, and this effect is particularly pronounced in high-tech industries and non-state-owned enterprises, indicating the moderating roles of ownership and industry attributes. These findings enrich the theoretical research at the intersection of behavioral finance and innovation economics, and provide practical implications for policymakers. We emphasize that optimizing resource allocation, improving corporate governance, and strengthening differentiated support can guide enterprises to control financialization risks while achieving high-quality innovative development.

title: Beyond Formal Employment: Collective Agency and Economic Inclusion among Deaf Young People in a Community-Based Batik Initiative
summary: Economic inclusion among Deaf young people is frequently assessed in terms of formal employment, overlooking collective opportunities to apply vocational skills and engage in income-generating activities. This study examined how a corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative facilitated collective agency and economic participation within NOSATA, a community-based batik group in Tangerang Regency, Indonesia. A qualitative case study was conducted through a secondary analysis of interview data and program documentation collected during the 2025 Social Return on Investment (SROI) evaluation of Bercerita Dalam Hening. Thematic analysis was employed to examine structural barriers, enabling conditions, capability development, collective agency, and economic participation from 2022 to 2025. The findings indicated that mentoring, a dedicated production workshop, production technologies, institutional partnerships, and market access opportunities facilitated the translation of vocational skills into productive economic activities. Group membership increased from five active participants to 41 members, while the number of batik trainers rose from zero in 2023 to 16 in 2025. Reported annual batik sales increased from IDR 30.4 million to IDR 71.7 million, while income generated from training activities rose from IDR 6 million to IDR 30 million. These developments suggested the emergence of collective agency through knowledge sharing, collaborative resource utilization, and engagement with external stakeholders. However, continued reliance on institutional support constrained claims regarding organizational autonomy and long-term economic independence. The study concluded that economic inclusion extends beyond formal employment to encompass collective entrepreneurship, skill utilization, and community-based economic participation.

title: Digital Competence and Employee Performance in Banking: The Mediating Role of Readiness to Change
summary: Digital transformation has changed work processes and demands, making digital competence a critical capability for supporting employee performance. This study aims to analyze and synthesize the relationship between digital competence, readiness to change, and employee performance, as well as to identify the potential of readiness to change as a mediating mechanism linking digital competence to employee performance. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) method through the identification, selection, and synthesis of articles relevant to the relationships among the variables. The findings indicate that digital competence contributes to employee performance through employees ability to utilize technology, adapt work processes to digital systems, and complete tasks more effectively. Digital competence is also related to an individual’s readiness to face change, although empirical evidence of this relationship remains limited, particularly in the banking sector. Furthermore, readiness to change plays a role in supporting employee performance by helping employees accept, adapt to, and maintain work effectiveness during organizational change. This study identifies mechanism gaps, integration gaps, and contextual gaps, and provides a conceptual foundation for positioning readiness to change as an adaptive mechanism in the relationship between digital competence and employee performance. These findings provide direction for future research to empirically test this integrated model, particularly in the context of digital transformation in the banking sector. title: The impact of technological anxiety on knowledge sharing behavior among older employees
summary: Purpose This study aims to explore the impact mechanism of technological anxiety among older employees on knowledge sharing behavior, as well as the roles of job crafting and relational energy and to test the moderating effect of organizational identity. Design/methodology/approach The samples used in the study are mainly from the survey data of older employees in enterprises under the background of China’s digital transformation. A total of 403 valid samples is obtained, including manufacturing, finance, information technology, public services and energy industries, as well as various types of organizations such as state-owned enterprises, private enterprises and foreign-funded enterprises. The samples have good structural distribution and industry representation. The partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) method was used to test the research model. Findings The results of an empirical survey reveal that technological anxiety significantly and negatively affects older employees’ knowledge sharing behavior, while job crafting and relational energy play a sequential mediating role. Moreover, organizational identification moderates the first stage of this chain mediation by buffering the negative impact of technological anxiety on job crafting. Originality/value The findings not only deepen the understanding of older employees’ knowledge sharing behavior in the context of digital transformation, but also expand the application of the job demands-resources framework and socioemotional selectivity theory in the research on technological anxiety among older employees.

title: Propuesta de un modelo de gestión documental basado en inteligencia artificial para instituciones públicas
summary: Document management has become a strategic pillar for the efficiency and transparency of public institutions, especially within the framework of digital transformation. Traditional models are insufficient to address the growing volume of information, demanding innovative approaches that guarantee authenticity, traceability, and timely access. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a transformative tool for archival processes. This study aimed to propose a conceptual model of document management based on AI, articulating three dimensions: regulatory, organizational, and technological. A qualitative-descriptive approach was adopted, combining documentary analysis of the theoretical and regulatory framework with semi-structured interviews with three public archives professionals. The data were processed using ATLAS.ti v.25, employing open coding to identify units of meaning, which were then grouped into integrating themes and higher-order analytical categories. The results revealed three central axes: legal, organizational, and technological. A word cloud generated from the textual corpus confirmed the relevance of these areas and the role of archives in public administration. It is concluded that an AI-driven document management model is viable and strategic, provided it is based on solid regulatory framework, adequate technological infrastructure, and personnel specialized in information management. This integration allows public institutions to align themselves with new information landscapes, strengthening accountability, preserving documentary heritage, and promoting a comprehensive and sustainable digital transformation.

title: Reflections on Digital Finance and Artificial Intelligence Driving Corporate Green Innovation Under the Background of Platform Economy
summary: In the process of advancing the dual carbon strategy, the integration of industrial digitalization and green low-carbon development has become a core direction for the transformation of the real economy, with green innovation serving as a key pathway for enterprises to overcome growth constraints and achieve low-carbon upgrades. Currently, domestic enterprises generally face practical challenges in their green transition, including capital shortages, slow technological iteration, and uneven distribution of innovation resources, making traditional development models inadequate to meet the demands of green industries. Leveraging the advantages of platform economies—such as data integration and supply chain connectivity—digital finance and artificial intelligence are gradually emerging as critical tools to support corporate green innovation. This paper examines the application scenarios within the platform economy, focusing on how digital and intelligent technologies empower green innovation, while identifying current issues such as fragmented industry data standards, significant disparities in enterprise transformation, lagging regulatory frameworks, and underdeveloped market mechanisms. Addressing these pain points, the study proposes improvement strategies in areas including data governance, support for small and micro enterprises, regulatory optimization, and the construction of an innovation ecosystem. The findings offer practical guidance for corporate low-carbon transitions and provide theoretical support for the integration of digital and green development, as well as regional low-carbon, high-quality growth.

title: Corporate Tax Behavior and Financial Characteristics: Evidence from Indonesian Consumer Non-Cyclical Firms
summary: Corporate tax behavior reflects how firms balance tax compliance, financial strategies, and governance considerations. This study examines the association between ownership structure, capital structure, profitability, and corporate tax behavior measured through the Cash Effective Tax Rate (CETR) among Indonesian consumer non-cyclical firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2021–2024. Using firm-year observations and pooled ordinary least squares regression, this study analyzes whether corporate characteristics are associated with firms’ cash tax positions. The findings indicate that institutional ownership is positively associated with CETR, suggesting that stronger institutional monitoring is related to higher cash tax payments and lower tax avoidance tendencies. Meanwhile, leverage, managerial ownership, debt reliance, and profitability do not show significant associations with corporate tax behavior. This study contributes to the corporate governance and taxation literature by highlighting the role of ownership mechanisms in explaining firms’ cash tax positions in an emerging market context

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled green recruitment and transformational leadership in strengthening small and medium-sized enterprise resilience: The mediating roles of work engagement and artificial intelligence utilisation
summary: Orientation: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in emerging economies increasingly face sustainability pressures and digital transformation demands that require adaptive human resource practices, effective leadership, and technology-enabled resilience. Research purpose: This study examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled green recruitment and transformational leadership in strengthening SME resilience through work engagement and AI utilisation. Motivation for the study: Prior research has examined green human resource management, leadership, and digital transformation separately; however, limited empirical evidence explains how behavioural and technological mechanisms jointly shape SMEs resilience. Research approach/design and method: A quantitative explanatory design was applied using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Data were collected through a structured questionnaire from 249 Indonesian SMEs owners and employees who had adopted digital practices in business processes or human resource management. Main findings: Artificial intelligence-enabled green recruitment and transformational leadership positively and significantly influenced work engagement, AI utilisation, and SME resilience. Work engagement and AI utilisation also strengthened SME resilience and mediated the effects of both antecedents on SMEs resilience. The behavioural pathway through work engagement showed a stronger contribution than the technological pathway. The model explained 79.0% of the variance in SMEs resilience. Practical/managerial implications: Small and medium-sized enterprises managers should integrate AI-enabled green recruitment with transformational leadership to enhance employee engagement, AI utilisation, and adaptive organisational behaviour. Contribution/value-add: This study contributes by integrating behavioural and technological mechanisms into a resilience framework for SMEs in an emerging economy context.

title: AIGC and total factor productivity in emerging-market media firms: mechanisms, heterogeneity, and industrial spillovers
summary: Using panel data of Chinese A-share listed media firms over 2013–2023, this study examines whether and how Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC) affects total factor productivity (TFP) in emerging markets. Employing instrumental variable and difference-in-differences identification strategies, we document that AIGC adoption significantly enhances media firms’ TFP. Technological innovation and resource allocation efficiency constitute dual mediating channels, with innovation quantitatively dominant. The productivity dividend is markedly stronger for small-scale, non-state-owned firms located in digitally advanced regions. AIGC drives both technological progress and technical efficiency, and generates positive industry spillovers along media value chains, informing digital transformation policies for emerging economies.

title: Technological Transformation: Implementation of the First Augmented Reality Application at PT XYZ
summary: The implementation of Augmented Reality (AR) technology at PT Rizky Megatama Sentosa marks an important step in the digital transformation of this cigarette company. AR is being implemented as a strategy to increase consumer engagement and strengthen innovative marketing campaigns. Through the AR application, consumers can access interactive content such as company information, 3D visuals, and information about the cigarette raw material process, providing a more personal and interesting experience. This article discusses the AR application development process, from identifying business needs to launch, as well as the challenges faced during implementation. The results of implementing AR show a significant increase in consumer engagement, brand loyalty and product sales. This study highlights how AR can be an effective tool to drive innovation and increase company competitiveness in the increasingly competitive cigarette industry.
