title: The Influence of Islamic Capital Market Education and Literacy on Students’ Investment Activity in Digital Sharia Investment Platforms
summary: Despite the growing number of students with sharia investment accounts, active participation in digital Islamic investment platforms remains limited indicating a gap between financial education and actual investment behavior. This study examines the influence of Islamic capital market education and literacy on students’ investment activity on digital sharia platforms. Using a quantitative explanatory approach, data were collected from 95 students in the fifth and seventh semesters of the Faculty of Islamic Economics and Business (FEBI) at UIN North Sumatra, selected through purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS version 27. The results show that Islamic capital market education has a positive but statistically non-significant effect on investment activity (β = 0.415; t = 1.726; Sig = 0.088). In contrast, Islamic capital market literacy has a positive and significant effect (β = 0.717; t = 3.274; Sig = 0.001), making it the most dominant predictor (standardized β = 0.463). Simultaneously, both variables significantly explain 46.5% of the variation in investment activity (F = 39.997; Sig= 0.000). These findings suggest that improving applied literacy not merely theoretical education is essential to stimulate active investment behavior, with practical implications for curriculum design, investment gallery programs, and Islamic fintech platform development targeting university students..

title: Towards the protection of shareholders' proposal rights in limited liability companies—From the perspective of the validity of shareholders' meeting resolution
summary: Though not explicitly established under the current Company Law, the shareholder proposal right constitutes a core entitlement for minority shareholders of limited liability companies to engage in corporate governance, and its potential exercise would directly bear on the validity of shareholders' meeting resolutions. Focusing on limited liability companies as the research subject, this paper integrates their characteristics of personal nexus and closedness to sort out the fundamental theories concerning the shareholder proposal right and the validity of shareholders' meeting resolutions. It further dissects procedural obstacles that would be encountered in the potential exercise of the shareholder proposal right, such as shareholding percentage thresholds and deficiencies in relief mechanisms, as well as the ensuing disputes over the validity of resolutions. In response to issues in judicial practice, including inconsistent criteria for identifying defects in the proposal right and ambiguous rules regarding the types of resolution validity, this paper puts forward paths for institutional construction of the shareholder proposal right from three dimensions: clarifying the rules governing the exercise of the proposal right, establishing standards for determining resolution validity, and designing judicial relief and dispute resolution mechanisms. This study provides theoretical reference and guidance for legislative supplementation and judicial rule-making concerning internal governance of limited liability companies.

title: VALUE RELEVANCE OF ACCOUNTING INFORMATION AND MARKET PRICE PER SHARE: EVIDENCE FROM LISTED CONGLOMERATES IN NIGERIA
summary: This study examines the value relevance of accounting information and the market value of listed Nigerian conglomerates over the period 2021–2025. The study is motivated by the continuing debate on the usefulness of accounting information in explaining market valuation, particularly within emerging capital markets where investors operate under varying levels of information efficiency. The study adopts an ex-post facto research design and uses secondary data extracted from the audited annual reports and financial statements of listed Nigerian conglomerates. Market value per share (MPS) serves as the dependent variable, while earnings per share (EPS) and book value per share (BVPS) constitute the explanatory variables. The study is anchored on Ohlson’s (1995) valuation framework and employs random effects panel regression techniques, as the appropriate estimator. The findings indicate that earnings per share and book value per share have positive and statistically significant relationships with market value per share, suggesting that investors incorporate both profitability and net asset information into their valuation decisions. The study concludes that accounting information remains value relevant among listed Nigerian conglomerates. It therefore recommends that management of listed conglomerates should strengthen the quality, transparency, accuracy, and timeliness of financial reporting, particularly the disclosure of earnings and shareholders’ equity information, to enhance investor confidence and support informed investment decisions

title: Pendampingan Tata Kelola Digital ‘Aisyiyah melalui Penguatan Manajemen dan Sinergi Lokal–Global
summary: The rapid advancement of digital technology requires community organizations to strengthen governance systems that are effective, transparent, and adaptive. This community service program aimed to enhance the digital governance capacity of ‘Aisyiyah through collaboration among Universitas Muhammadiyah Jambi, the Regional Leadership of ‘Aisyiyah Jambi, and the Special Branch Leadership of ‘Aisyiyah New South Wales, Australia. The program employed socialization, training, mentoring, and evaluation methods to support the implementation of digital-based organizational administration, communication, documentation, and website-based information management. The results demonstrated significant improvements in participants’ knowledge and skills in utilizing digital technologies to improve organizational governance. Furthermore, the collaboration between local and international partners facilitated the exchange of best practices and strengthened the sustainability of organizational digital transformation. This program provides a practical model for assisting community organizations in achieving modern, professional, and sustainable digital governance.

title: Does the rural digital economy enhance green total factor productivity of agriculture? An empirical approach using double machine learning
summary: Introduction In the context of the green transformation of agriculture, the digital economy offers a novel pathway to mitigate environmental externalities and operational inefficiencies. Recognizing that agricultural digitalisation relies heavily on the spillover of macro-level digital resources, this study constructs a multidimensional rural digital economy (RDE) framework. Methods Employing a double machine learning (DML) model on a panel dataset of 30 Chinese provinces from 2011 to 2022, we empirically investigate the impact of the RDE on agricultural green total factor productivity (GTFP). Results We find that: (1) The RDE exerts a positive effect on GTFP. Dimensional analysis strictly confirms that digital industry development and industrial digital transformation have positive linkages with this productivity growth, whereas basic infrastructure alone is insufficient. (2) Mechanism analyses demonstrate that the RDE empowers green agriculture by optimizing inter-sectoral factor allocation and significantly reducing agricultural polluting energy intensity; however, the mediating role of government digital policy attention is not statistically established. (3) To accurately capture asymmetric effects, group-based heterogeneity tests reveal that the empowerment effect of the RDE is significantly stronger in provinces with larger cultivated scales. Discussion These findings indicate that the RDE currently empowers green agriculture primarily through structural factor reallocation and precision energy management rather than immediate technological leaps. To overcome hardware-software structural lags and mitigate scale disadvantages faced by smallholders, policymakers should pivot toward enhancing farmers’ digital literacy, expanding shared digital socialized services, and implementing market-based environmental governance.

title: The Effect of Perceived Usefulness of the Tring Application and Digital Service Quality on Customer Loyalty through Customer Satisfaction at PT Pegadaian, Mamuju Branch
summary: Digital transformation in the financial services sector has encouraged PT Pegadaian to develop the TRING application as a digital service platform to enhance customer satisfaction and loyalty. This study aims to analyze the effects of perceived usefulness of the TRING application and digital service quality on customer loyalty through customer satisfaction at PT Pegadaian, Mamuju Branch. This study employed a quantitative approach using a survey of 100 respondents who use the TRING application. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with the assistance of SmartPLS software. The results indicate that: (1) perceived usefulness of the TRING application has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction; (2) digital service quality has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction; (3) perceived usefulness of the TRING application has a positive but insignificant effect on customer loyalty; (4) digital service quality has a positive and significant effect on customer loyalty; (5) customer satisfaction has a positive but insignificant effect on customer loyalty; (6) perceived usefulness of the TRING application does not have a significant effect on customer loyalty through customer satisfaction; and (7) digital service quality does not have a significant effect on customer loyalty through customer satisfaction. The findings indicate that digital service quality is the most dominant factor in enhancing the loyalty of TRING application users, while customer satisfaction does not yet function as a mediating variable in the research model. Therefore, PT Pegadaian should prioritize improving digital service quality, particularly in terms of system reliability, security, ease of use, and service responsiveness, to strengthen customer loyalty.

title: Efektivitas Implementasi Transformasi Digital Rekam Medis Elektronik
summary: Electronic medical record (EMR) implementation in regional hospitals still faces technological, human resource, and governance challenges, while HOT-Fit-based studies in regional hospitals remain limited. This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of EMR digital transformation, its supporting and inhibiting factors, and its impact on service effectiveness at Arosuka Regional Hospital, Solok Regency. A qualitative case study approach was used. Five informants were selected purposively through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation, analyzed thematically using NVivo 15 within the HOT-Fit framework. The results show that 20 of 24 service units (83.33%) actively use the EMR, with easier recording, information access, and service efficiency. Waiting times improved to under 60 minutes. However, user competence is uneven, training is not routine, usage across units is inconsistent, and network disruptions persist. It is concluded that EMR implementation is fairly effective but not yet optimal, and Net Benefit will be maximized when the Human, Organization, and Technology dimensions are aligned.

title: Malaysia's Economic Transformation: Growth, Fiscal Reform, Digital Industries and Inclusive Prosperity
summary: Abstract: Malaysia’s economy in 2026 combines resilient domestic demand, strong export-oriented manufacturing and rapid investment in digital infrastructure with continuing exposure to external shocks. Official data show that real gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 6.0% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, led by services, manufacturing, exports and investment, while headline inflation rose to 1.9% as fuel costs linked to the Middle East conflict fed through. The government’s fiscal planning for 2027 must balance household protection, energy security, development spending and medium-term fiscal consolidation. This conceptual review examines Malaysia’s economic transformation through five themes: the composition of growth, fiscal sustainability, productivity and wages, digital and high-value industries, and inclusive development. Drawing on research on the middle-income trap, foreign direct investment spillovers, subsidy targeting and global value chains, it argues that headline growth must be judged alongside productivity, real wage progression, regional opportunity, business dynamism and environmental sustainability. The paper proposes a seven-part policy framework that links investment attraction to domestic supplier development, skills formation, innovation diffusion, targeted social protection and transparent public finance. It also sets out research priorities on the quality of digital investment, the distribution of productivity gains and the long-term effects of subsidy and tax reform. The paper is a policy-oriented conceptual review and does not estimate original econometric relationships. title: PROSPECTS FOR THE APPLICATION OF CLOUD COMPUTING IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF MODERN INFORMATION SYSTEMS
summary: This article examines the prospects for the application of cloud computing in the development of modern information systems. The study aims to identify the architectural, economic, and organizational factors influencing the effectiveness of cloud adoption and to propose a phased model for migrating information systems to cloud environments. The research methodology integrates a comparative analysis of scientific literature and policy documents, a systems-based approach, and a criteria-based qualitative assessment of cloud service and deployment models. The findings suggest that significant benefits can be achieved by integrating cloud services with microservices architecture, container orchestration, serverless computing components, and edge computing technologies. Particular attention is given to information security, data sovereignty, and vendor lock-in as key considerations in the planning and implementation of cloud solutions. Based on the analysis, a seven-stage cloud migration model and a set of evaluation criteria for selecting appropriate cloud solutions are proposed. The findings may provide practical guidance for public- and private-sector organizations seeking to modernize their information systems, enhance operational efficiency, and support sustainable digital transformation.
